name: vicious mockery
lore:
# On the Art of the Barbed Tongue: Vicious Mockery

To weave this cantrip is to pull the Arcanum into a jagged, needle-thin point. To the caster, it feels like the copper tang of blood on the tongue or the cold prickle of a winter wind against a raw nerve. It is a precise, acidic manipulation of the Weave, demanding more spite than mana.

When unleashed, the air shimmers with a violet, discordant haze. The target does not merely hear an insult; they feel the magic manifest as a psychic lash—a phantom weight that buckles the knees and clouds the vision with a crushing sense of inadequacy.

Legend attributes its discovery to Elara the Mute, a court jester who, after being magically silenced by a cruel Duke, channeled her bottled indignity into a single, devastating smirk. The Duke collapsed, his ego shattered by the sheer weight of her unvoiced contempt. Since that day, the "Barbed Tongue" has remained the favorite tool of the wit-quick, proving that a well-placed jibe, when laced with the Weave, cuts deeper than forged steel.
